justification: A uses a serif face with comfortable leading and generous margins, which reads as a refined, book-like document (A2-A4). Its last page is mostly empty (A5), and the thin top rule is a weaker running frame. B has a bold sans, running header and footer bands with section names and page counts, and fuller pages with even rhythm (B2-B4). Its text is denser and justified with wider word gaps, and the heavy bands feel more corporate. A's nicer typography and breathing room edge out B's better page balance.

A flows continuously: Etymology and History start mid-page with the images placed well, and the serif body has generous leading with clean, unobtrusive footers (A4, A5). B leaves a big blank area under the Etymology image (B4) and spends a full page on a History divider with a sidebar (B5). B's heavy header and footer bands add chrome, and its justified text shows rivers and awkward word spacing in the bullet items (B8). B's dividers and bands are bold and well made, but they cost pagination and rhythm. A's table of contents page numbers look slightly off against the content, but that is minor.

A has a bold navy cover and header/footer bands that give a stronger identity. Its heading hierarchy is clearer, with section titles over rules and bold subheads. B is a clean serif layout with numbered headings and a centered cover, but it feels plainer. A's map page is mostly empty, and B's text flows better into the map page. Overall A is more polished.

Design A leaves large empty areas. A5 holds only an image and caption with the rest blank, and A3, A4 and A8 are mostly empty. It also splits sections across pages and mixes indents with drop caps unevenly. Design B flows continuously, with full-width images and consistent header and footer bands. It has a steady rhythm and fuller pages. Its headings are lighter than A's, but the overall reading experience is more cohesive.

A flows continuously over 6 pages. Images sit with their text, and the header and footer bands give consistent navigation. B has large empty areas: B3 is half blank, B5 holds only an image on an empty page, and B4 and B6 have big top gaps. B's drop caps are inconsistent, the indents are awkward, and the text blocks are misaligned with the headings. A is more cohesive and denser, though A's headings are plainer.

B packs content more evenly: the image on B4 sits above the Thermal energy section, so the page is not left mostly empty. A4 is a lone image with a large blank page, and A5 starts with a big blank top margin. B's header and footer bands give consistent navigation and structure. A's serif body with drop caps and bolder headings is elegant, but the drop caps are inconsistent and the blank pages hurt the rhythm. B's section headings are light and slightly weak, but the overall flow is steadier.

A has a striking full-bleed blue cover and a nice drop-cap treatment, but its pagination leaves large empty areas: A4 holds only a photo with the rest blank, A7 holds only the map, and A3 and A6 end early. The result is choppy and wasteful. B flows continuously, with images placed near the text, numbered headings, and consistent running headers and footers. Its density is even and it reads as a coherent document. B's cover is plainer, but the body pages are more polished.

A has a clear system: header and footer bands, numbered headings, and a sidebar section-divider page (A5) that gives strong hierarchy and identity. Its main weakness is large empty areas on pages such as A4, A5 and A2, with sparse pages and a page 9 missing from the sequence. B is clean, continuous and tightly paginated, with a pleasant serif, but its flow is plainer. Headings are weaker, with little differentiation between sections, and there are no bands or dividers beyond a thin top rule. B also has a few awkward breaks, such as a heading near the page bottom on B5. A feels more designed and easier to navigate.

A uses a refined serif with generous margins and leading, plus a table of contents (A2) and clear section rules and headings (A4, A5). B's sans body text is justified with wider tracking and loose word spacing, and its heavy header and footer bands feel mechanical, though they aid navigation (B2-B6). The images are about equal, with B's slightly wider. A leaves a mostly empty TOC page, a small cost.

A uses a serif body with numbered section headings that start pages and sit in clear spaces (A3, A4). Its text is comfortable to read, though several pages end with large empty areas (A5). B has a sans body and denser pages, with headings that run straight on from the preceding text (B2, B3). B's running header also shows the wrong section names, for example 'Antiquity' on a page with intro text. B's body is tight and wall-like, which makes it harder to scan.

A uses navy header and footer bands carrying the running title, section name and 'Page X of 4'. Its sans-serif bold subheads are clear, and its pages are filled consistently (A2-A4). B's serif body is elegant, but the thin top rule is weak. B also ends on a near-empty page 5 with a few orphaned lines (B5), and its page 3 has a gap at the bottom. B's cover is darker and plainer, with the accent line barely visible (B1).

A has a coherent system: running header and footer bands, a table of contents, a sidebar section divider (A5), numbered headings, and images that sit with their text (A6). B's drop caps are misaligned and its indents are inconsistent; its heading and body left edges do not match (B3, B4, B6). B also leaves page 5 almost empty, with the image stranded and separated from its text (B5). A's page 8 is dense, but it reads cleanly.

B has a table of contents (B2), a banded section divider (B5) and a serif body, so it reads as a more complete, polished document. Its weak points are a large blank area under the image on B4 and a bullet list split across pages (B7-B8). A is compact with a sans body and clear section rules, but it has no TOC or dividers and large empty space on A6. A's text-and-image flow (A3, A4) is tidier, but A feels more plain overall.

B uses bold sans headings that stand out clearly against the serif body (B3, B4). Its drop caps add some interest, though the wrapped lines beside them are awkward (B3, B5). B also starts sections on fresh pages and keeps the text blocks tidy. A has a cleaner, more consistent serif system, but its headings are small and weak, and the final page holds only a few lines (A5). A's running header rule is a plain touch. A's dark cover is elegant, while B's cover is flatter and more generic. Overall B has stronger hierarchy and navigation.

A pairs a serif body with a bold sans heading. Its numbered headings (1 Potential, 2.1 Early commercial adaptation) make a clear hierarchy, and the text is easy to read (A2, A4). B's light-weight sans body is thin, and its section headings are light and no more prominent than the body text. B does have a strong navy cover and navy header and footer bands, but the cover is left-aligned in a large empty field, and the heavy bands feel more imposing than useful (B1, B2). B's pages fill more evenly, while A leaves a large gap on A3 and A6. Overall A reads better and looks more refined.

A uses bold sans headings, drop-cap openers and running section footers, so sections are easy to find (A3, A4). Its cover has a brighter blue and stronger title (A1). B has serif headings that are only slightly larger than the body, and a thin rule at the top of each page. Sections break mid-page, and the last page is nearly empty (B5). B's lines are long and dense, though its pages are fuller. A's pages end with some uneven gaps and A5 is also sparse.

A has a table of contents (A2), a sidebar-band History divider (A5), numbered section headings and a serif body that reads well (A3, A7). Its weaknesses are large empty areas on A2, A4 and A5, and the page numbering skips from 4 to 6 in the pages shown. B is compact and continuous. Its sans body and flat headings are weaker, headings are small, and sections run on mid-page without breaks (B3, B4). B has no contents page and no divider bands.

A uses sans-serif section headings with numbering and header/footer bands carrying the section name and 'Page X of 5' (A2-A5), giving clear navigation and stronger hierarchy. B's headings are only slightly larger serif text and its body is denser, so sections blend together (B3, B4). B's last page holds only a few lines (B5). A's last page is also sparse, but its sections are better separated. A's body is justified with a slightly larger size, which makes it easier to read.

A uses a serif body with a geometric bold sans for headings, and its drop caps and section starts give clear hierarchy and pacing. Roomy margins and a light footer help it read well. B is dense and uniform, with heavy header and footer bands. Its headings sit mid-page and the running header says 'Antiquity' on a page that opens with intro text, which confuses navigation. A leaves some pages short, but that reads as deliberate section breaks.

A has numbered headings in a bold sans and a clear header and footer. Its image sits with the text it relates to, so pages fill more evenly (A4, A6). B has a bold full-bleed blue cover (B1), which is its strength, and drop caps. But its image strands alone on a mostly empty page (B4), and the map page is also largely empty (B7). Its heading levels are less distinct, and its running footers are weaker. A is more cohesive and flows better.

A uses an elegant serif with a thin top rule and a quiet footer, and its headings are clear and unnumbered. B has heavy header and footer bands, redundant numbering such as '1 Antiquity', and justified text with wide word gaps. A's last page is mostly empty, but B's last page is also sparse. A's text flows continuously across pages, while B leaves large gaps at the bottom of its pages.

A uses clean section headings and blue drop caps that add editorial character. Its margins are generous and it has light running footers. B's heavy navy header and footer bands feel mechanical and crowd the pages. B's numbered headings ("1 Antiquity") are redundant, and its dense text blocks have little variation. A's drop caps are slightly awkward in places, but overall A reads more elegantly.

B uses a serif face with generous line spacing and a table of contents (B2), so it reads like a book and is comfortable over long text. A's sans text is dense and justified with tight leading, with rivers visible (A2, A5). A's navy header and footer bands give clear navigation but crowd the page. A's images sit tighter to the text and the pages are fuller, though A6 ends with a big empty area. B's pages are airier and more consistent (B3-B7). B's bold headings are clear, and its cover is slightly muted.

B reads as a finished document. It has a table of contents, header and footer bands, a bold History divider page with a side index, and images that sit with their text (B4, B6). A leaves large empty areas: A5 holds only a floating image and A8 is half blank. Its pages are inconsistent, and a few drop caps look awkward (A4, A6). A's headings and drop caps give some character, but its inconsistent margins and wasted pages weaken it. B's text is dense, though, and the TOC page is mostly empty.

A runs the text continuously across pages with a clean sans body and unnumbered headings, and its pages are filled evenly (A2-A4). B forces a break before each section, leaving large empty areas at the bottom of B2, B3 and B5. B's numbered headings ("1 Antiquity") and serif body feel less refined. Both have the same header and footer bands and the same cover.

A reads as a consistent, well-paced document. It has a table of contents, a top band on each page, and a single serif family with clean heading rules. Images sit with their text and pages fill sensibly (A4, A5). B has dropcaps that break the line alignment, and the Etymology text is indented while its image is not. B also leaves large empty areas, such as B5, which holds only an image, and B3 and B8, which are mostly blank. Its headings float oddly after blank space at the top of pages, and its margins and indents are inconsistent. B's bold sans headings are stronger, but its overall rhythm is weaker.

Design A has navy header and footer bands with running titles and page numbers, plus numbered headings (A2-A5). The bands frame the pages well, but the numbered headings are cramped and the text is justified, which leaves a loose gap at the bottom of each page. Design B has a more refined heading face, drop caps that open sections, and a quieter footer (B3-B5). Its text flows continuously across pages, so the page fill is fuller and the rhythm better. The drop caps are slightly awkward, because the indent wraps oddly and the lines are misaligned (B3, B4, B5). Overall B reads as the more polished and readable document.

A uses a sans body in dense, full pages with header and footer bands, so it is consistent and compact. Its headings sit at page bottoms and its text is cramped (A2, A3). B has a serif body, roomy margins and drop caps, but the drop caps are awkwardly spaced (B3, B5). Its pages end with uneven empty space (B2, B5). Overall, B is the more pleasant read, though A's running header bands are a plus.

A leaves large empty areas: A3 has half a page blank under the image, A5 holds only an image with a caption, and A8 is mostly empty. Its section starts are forced onto separate pages, with inconsistent indents and drop caps that do not match the headings. B flows continuously, with consistent margins, a top band on each page and a table of contents on B2. Its images sit well with their text on B4 and B5, and its page rhythm is steady. A's sans headings and drop caps give some character, but its pagination is wasteful.

A uses header and footer bands that give clear navigation and a consistent frame (A2-A6). Its image sits with the Thermal energy heading on A4, so the page is well filled. B has a nearly empty image page (B4) and a half-empty page (B5) that starts with a large gap above the heading. B's drop caps are uneven and misaligned with the paragraph indents (B2, B6). B's serif body is pleasant, but it has no bands and looser pagination. A's justified text has some wide spacing, and its page 3 and 6 are partly empty, but overall A flows better.
